text: Miss Cheng Li Hui in her Budget Speech yesterday, and Ms Denise Phua and Ms Ng Ling Ling in their speeches today, have suggested increasing support for Singaporeans who undergo Assisted Conception Procedures, or ACPs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agree that adequate financial and socio-emotional support is important.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While we encourage married couples to have children when they are younger and their chances are better, we have also enhanced ACP support over the years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The age cap on ACP co-funding is based on clinical evidence that success rates decrease with age.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In deciding the maximum number of co-funded cycles, we also considered the emotional strain couples face when undergoing ACPs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With MediSave and existing co-funding support, eight in 10 eligible Singaporean couples have no out-of-pocket expenses for their first cycle, while nine in 10 would not pay more than $500 for their first cycle.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Just last year, we removed the age limit for women undergoing Assisted Reproduction Technology, or ART, treatments.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also enhanced the co-funding scheme for couples to tap on up to two of the six co-funded ART cycles when the wife is aged 40 and above, if she had attempted an ACP before 40.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to review the MediSave withdrawal limits to balance between supporting couples with their cost of treatment today, and ensuring they have sufficient savings for healthcare in old age.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While public Assisted Reproduction centres currently provide couples undergoing ACP with emotional support and social counselling, we will do more with community partners to provide holistic support and remove stigma for those seeking fertility checks or treatment.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Hany Soh, who has asked for information to be disseminated to first-time parents, will be glad to know that the MSF's Baby Bonus Parenting Resources, or BBPR, Pregnancy Keepsake Journal, provides tips on pregnancy and parenthood.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will be piloted at maternity hospitals and selected private obstetrics clinics, complementing MSF's BBPR website, and HPB's e-toolkits for expectant mothers and new parents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members may also access these materials through the SG PARL MP mobile app.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While most married Singaporeans wish to have two or more children, and the majority still do, a growing number have only one child.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some Singaporean couples have shared their worries about the costs of having a second child, even though they very much want to.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Currently, the support from Government to parents for their second child is the same as their first.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is in addition to the $3,000 CDA First Step Grant that parents receive upon opening the CDA.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The one-time $200 CDA top-up, announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng on Budget Day, as part of the Household Support Package, will provide additional support.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Carrie Tan has championed greater gender equality in caring for children and asked to set aside two months from the current four months of maternity leave, as paternity leave.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She also asked for tax incentives to nudge fathers to use them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agree that the active involvement of fathers is critical to the wellbeing of children and their partners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, fathers can already share up to one month of their wives' maternity leave under the Shared Parental Leave Scheme, on top of two weeks of paternity leave.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, only about 5% of fathers use this flexibility.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some couples also prefer to reserve all 16 weeks of maternity leave for mothers to recuperate and bond with their child.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, we are cautious about requiring fathers to take more of mothers' existing maternity leave.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We would first urge fathers to take their paternity leave.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since the introduction of Paternity Leave, take-up rates have increased from 25% in 2013 to 53% in 2018.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is encouraging that more fathers have been taking time off to care for their new-borns, and we hope this signals a stronger shift towards greater shared parental responsibility.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some working fathers and adoptive mothers may not qualify for paternity or adoption leave due to their employment arrangements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, they may be on multiple short-term employment contracts, or their employment contracts may have expired before the birth or adoption of their child.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is similar to the current Government-Paid Maternity Benefit for working mothers, where a cash benefit is given in lieu of the Government-paid share of leave if their employment circumstances do not qualify them for leave.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will apply to parents whose children's date of birth, estimated date of delivery, or formal intent to adopt, is on or after 1 January 2021.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: About 500 working fathers and adoptive mothers would benefit from GPPB and GPAB annually.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More details on the eligibility criteria and application process will be shared later.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I move on now to a workforce with a strong Singaporean Core.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The pandemic has also given us an opportunity to transform our workforce and reduce our reliance on lower skilled foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From June 2019 to June 2020, our total population declined slightly by 0.3% due to a decrease in foreign employment in the services sector, and Work Permit holders.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: S Pass and Employment Pass (EP) holders have also decreased amid the pandemic due to travel restrictions and the economic downturn.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government continues to maintain a tight stance on our foreign worker manpower policy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: COVID-19 has accelerated efforts for businesses to transform business models and improve productivity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, we will continue to partner businesses to train and retain local workers and strengthen the Singaporean Core of our workforce.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must also remain open to global talent who can complement our local workforce and attract high-value activities that create quality jobs for locals.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is why we have tightened the EP criteria and sharpened our tools, such as the Tech@SG and the Tech.Pass.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We set a high bar for these schemes and are very selective.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The talent base will help us emerge stronger, by anchoring and expanding new growth sectors.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Mr Timo Recker and Mr Andre Menezes, from Germany and Brazil, co-founded agri-food tech start-up Next Gen Foods in Singapore in early 2020.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They bring with them experience in alternative protein and food distribution.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The team is developing plant-based foods, including an alternative chicken product.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next Gen Food Technologist Ms Claudia Lee, who majored in Food Science at NUS, said it was a dream come true to work directly with leading global experts in plant-based foods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By working with global talent, more Singaporeans like Claudia can deepen their expertise in growth areas.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, safe management measures resulted in limited slots to complete the final steps for PR and citizenship registration, which must be done in-person.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, a few thousand applicants, who were approved in-principle, had not completed all the required processes to be granted their PR or citizenship respectively by end-2020.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Depending on how the COVID-19 situation evolves, these applicants could be granted PR or citizenship in the coming months and may add to the numbers normally granted this year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We continue to carefully select new PRs and citizens, and welcome those who have committed to making Singapore their home.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We take in immigrants not just based on their ability to contribute to Singapore, but also their ability to integrate.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Ms Denise Phua has acknowledged, foreign spouses have family ties to Singapore and our policies are already facilitative for those in genuine and stable marriages.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They can also qualify for a Letter of Consent from MOM which will allow them to work and care for their Singaporean children here.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must continue to build a community that is inclusive and united.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the past year, we saw many uplifting positive examples of Singaporeans and foreigners rallying together to help battle the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Ms Chong Pek Lian from Malaysia contributed to the COVID-19 battle as a contact tracer at Sengkang General Hospital.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Despite the long hours and heavy workload, she was glad to help reduce the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singaporeans also gave help, support and appreciation for our foreign workers who have contributed to our society, such as those in healthcare and construction.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many have continued to carry out their duties here and have not been able to see their families throughout this period.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our society will be stronger if all who call Singapore home and believe in our vision are empowered to make Singapore a better place.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will continue to work with a range of stakeholders to build our future together and emerge stronger post-COVID.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have consulted Singaporeans widely on population-related issues.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, in 2019, we convened a Citizens' Panel to tackle the tricky issue of improving work-life harmony, which affects marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2020, we also worked with the Citizens' Workgroup to co-develop new curriculum and programmes for the Singapore Citizenship Journey.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This initiative explored what it means to be Singaporean, including our shared values and duty to contribute to society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agree with Miss Cheng Li Hui that the Government's strategies for encouraging marriage and parenthood need to account for shifts in life priorities and societal norms.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As part of the Emerging Stronger Conversations, Minister of State Sun Xueling and I will lead a series of conversations on "Building A Singapore Made For Families", from April to September this year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We want to better understand how the thinking and aspirations of Singaporeans, at different stages of their Marriage and Parenthood journey, may have changed due to the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Denise Phua will be glad to know that the engagements will include transnational families, who may face unique challenges after deciding to make Singapore home.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will work together with the rest of society to better support all families in Singapore and shape an environment in which we can make time for things that matter.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our post-COVID world will require population strategies that keep us resilient and cohesive.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Together, let us continue to build a Singapore that is a home for all Singaporeans and emerge stronger as a nation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I think he made some general comments at the start about the status of corruption, and I just wanted to refer to the CPIB Report for 2019.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Singh asked for update on two cases.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I think it was the Keppel Offshore and Marine and I believe FAS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On Keppel Offshore and Marine, this case is complex and transnational, involving multiple authorities and potential foreign witnesses from several countries.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Singapore authorities have been working closely with foreign investigating and prosecuting agencies on the matter.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As part of the on-going investigation, AGC and CPIB had made two fact-finding trips to Brazil in May and August 2019.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: AGC and CPIB are also working together to send more MLA requests to other relevant foreign authorities to interview these potential witnesses.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While our intention is to move as expeditiously as possible, not all aspects of the investigation are within our control, particularly in relation to the requests and applications made and filed in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The current COVID-19 situation globally has also made the cross-jurisdiction investigation efforts more challenging.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: CPIB is unable to comment further on the case, so as to protect the integrity of investigations, which are confidential in nature and to avoid prejudicing any prosecutorial decision that might follow.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: CPIB remains resolute and committed to combat corruption and will continue to pursue the case to its end.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With respect to the FAS case, I am afraid that when Mr Pritam Singh filed the cut on corruption, normally you have to indicate the gist of the cut.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And the gist of the cut which is indicated to Parliament and then given to the Ministries, only indicated update on Keppel investigations; so, I am sorry I do not have the information on FAS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But perhaps, Mr Singh might like to file a Parliamentary Question on that.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, let me thank Mr Murali for recognising the efforts of CPIB in keeping corruption at bay.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Corruption is under control in Singapore but we must never be complacent.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The findings from CPIB's 2020 Public Perception Survey saw strong public confidence in our national anti-corruption efforts, with the following cited as the top three success factors contributing to the low corruption rate in Singapore: first, the political determination to keep corruption at bay; second, the heavy punishments; and third, the anti-corruption laws that are effective.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Prevention of Corruption Act has served Singapore well and remains an effective instrument.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: CPIB will provide more information on the review when it is ready together with AGC.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But having said that, Mr Speaker, Sir, I think I would like to emphasise one particular point that has come up from the various threads.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And that is, our reputation as a clean and corruption-free country is hard-won and is not something that we take for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Looking at our history, we know that such things may happen now and then, involving all strata of society.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But regardless of who is involved, which organisation is involved, nobody will be above the law and CPIB, together with the rest of the enforcement agencies will get to the bottom of each and every case, because the reputation of Singapore, the kind of values that we exhibit must be above all other considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, it is a hard-fought reputation, it is hard-won but we must never be complacent because it is a job that will never be done and we must never let our guard down.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Next, I will address the cuts from Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Melvin Yong on the Public Service's efforts to enhance employability, employment practices and build capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They came from all age groups, including mature workers, and we remain committed to supporting the needs of workers through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills effort.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Melvin Yong spoke about supporting public officers' lifelong employability, through good workforce and workplace practices.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Key to this is re-skilling our officers to continually upgrade their skillsets to keep up with the new job demands.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Since 2019, we have worked with the unions to upskill thousands of officers in areas such as basic digital literacy, data analytics and adapting to career and work-life transitions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are also developing public officers through job rotations and attachments to the private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Officers learn best practices to bring back to the public sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So far, we have worked with over 50 partners to attach over 90 officers from more than 30 agencies to such organisations and we will continue to expand this scheme further.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mid-career hires into the Civil Service also accounted for over 45% of all hires in the past five years.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We welcome more mid-career hires to join us and contribute their skillsets and experiences to public sector work.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are implementing progressive workplace practices to build a more collaborative and caring Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have implemented flexible work arrangements like enabling more officers to adopt hybrid work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are doing more to promote workplace health and mental wellness.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For instance, we are starting a Service-wide programme to train mental wellness ambassadors to provide peer support and care for co-workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are also making concerted efforts to strengthen the Public Service’s capability to serve Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have been investing in technology as a key driver of Public Sector Transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of our COVID-19 responses were underpinned by technology, like A*STAR and TTSH’s Fortitude test-kit, and HTX’s autonomous robot M.A.T.A.R deployed to patrol dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are leveraging technology like Artificial Intelligence (AI) for policy-making, service delivery and operations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The MSO One Service App uses AI-enabled routing of residents’ feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Public officers working in science, technology and engineering (STE) roles will be developed in niche areas like power engineering, modelling and simulation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We welcome more aspiring scientists and engineers into the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, we will increase the porosity between the Public Service and the private and people sector, so that we can gather experiences from all across the nation for the good of our country.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I agree with the Minister that flexible work arrangement especially work-from-home is the way forward.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Chairman, on the first question, I do not have information on specific study with me at hand but I can look that up and we will liaise with the Member separately.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the second, I believe the Member had a suggestion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am always happy to entertain suggestions from the hon Member Mr Louis Ng and we will look at it.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Chairman, I just have a clarification for Minister Indranee.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I was asking for a bit more flexibility and more liberalisation of the immigration policy for the foreign spouses of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Because if so, by the time they can apply for PR will be actually quite late.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And many of them would have Singaporean roots and the children and the families would all be here.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I think it would make sense to provide them the PR or citizenship status.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I was actually simply describing the broad range of measures.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Tin, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Chairman, I thank everyone for the contributions and also to our very hardworking Public Service officers and our leaders in this House for keeping Singapore vibrant and safe.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: With that, Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
